zinc differentially blocks GABA(A) responses in a region-specific manner in the thalamo-cortical system and that this blockade may have functional consequences on thalamo-corticocortical rhythmic activity.

zinc is released from nerve terminals throughout the thalamocortex system, where it blocks GABAergic inhibition in a region-specific manner, which may contribute to modulation of thalamocortically generated oscillations.

zinc is localized in the thalamus, nucleus reticularis, and neocortex, that zinc is released during thalamocortial (TC) activity, that exogenous application of zinc blocks TC rhythms and differentiates GABA(A) receptors within the TC system, that endogenously-released zinc is likely to be a neuromodulator of TC rhythmic activity, and that zinc is a potential treatment target for seizure disorders.

the modulation of GABAR-mediated synaptic inhibition by zinc in neurons of the thalamocortex system.
